The [United States Office of Management and Budget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Office_of_Management_and_Budget "United States Office of Management and Budget") (OMB) has defined 935 [core-based statistical areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core-based_statistical_area "Core-based statistical area") (CBSAs) for the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and 10 for [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_core-based_statistical_areas#cite_note-OMB_23-01-1) The OMB defines a core-based statistical area as one or more adjacent [counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)") or [county equivalents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States)#County_equivalents "County (United States)") that have at least one [urban core area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_urban_areas "List of United States urban areas") of at least 10,000 population, plus adjacent territory that has a high degree of social and economic integration with the core as measured by commuting ties. The 935 core-based statistical areas currently defined by the OMB include the 393 [metropolitan statistical areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area") (MSAs),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_core-based_statistical_areas#cite_note-MSA-2) which have an urban core population of at least 50,000, and the 542 [micropolitan statistical areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micropolitan_statistical_area "Micropolitan statistical area") (μSAs),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_core-based_statistical_areas#cite_note-%CE%BCSA-3) which have an urban core population of at least 10,000 but less than 50,000.

The [United States Office of Management and Budget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Office_of_Management_and_Budget "United States Office of Management and Budget") (OMB) has defined 935 [core-based statistical areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core-based_statistical_area "Core-based statistical area") (CBSAs) for the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and 10 for [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_core-based_statistical_areas#cite_note-OMB_23-01-1) The OMB defines a core-based statistical area as one or more adjacent [counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)") or [county equivalents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States)#County_equivalents "County (United States)") that have at least one [urban core area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_urban_areas "List of United States urban areas") of at least 10,000 population, plus adjacent territory that has a high degree of social and economic integration with the core as measured by commuting ties. The 935 core-based statistical areas currently defined by the OMB include the 393 [metropolitan statistical areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area") (MSAs),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_core-based_statistical_areas#cite_note-MSA-2) which have an urban core population of at least 50,000, and the 542 [micropolitan statistical areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micropolitan_statistical_area "Micropolitan statistical area") (μSAs),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_core-based_statistical_areas#cite_note-%CE%BCSA-3) which have an urban core population of at least 10,000 but less than 50,000.
